page: Microsoft Azure M624s_12_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MSHighMemoryv3 series, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization platform. The architecture is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors providing 624 dedicated vCPUs alongside 11,400 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a high memory allocation ratio of approximately 18.27 GB of RAM per vCPU, addressing scenarios where active data sets exceed typical scale-out limits.

The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators. Storage architecture relies on network-attached storage through Azure Premium Storage support for data persistence and operating system volumes. Network integration relies on private virtual networking, as no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned by default.

Resource allocation represents an extreme consolidation tier, trading horizontal distribution complexity for monolithic memory scale. Tradeoffs include heavy reliance on remote storage I/O bandwidth for persistence and high operational investment per node. The hardware configuration fits massive in-memory relational databases, SAP HANA production deployments, large-scale enterprise resource planning platforms, and intensive in-memory data processing systems.
description: Microsoft Azure M624s_12_v3 is a dedicated memory-optimized instance from the MSHighMemoryv3 family, deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system provides 624 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs paired with 11,400 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 18.27 GB of system memory per vCPU core. It operates without bundled local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, requiring attached Azure Premium Storage disks for operating system and application storage layers. Network architecture excludes complimentary public IPv4 addresses, expecting standard private virtual network topologies. The instance targets enterprise deployments requiring monolithic compute and expansive active memory address space without splitting state across distributed nodes. Workloads suited for this hardware footprint include hyperscale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, large-scale transaction processing systems, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise resource planning platforms processing multi-terabyte datasets in volatile memory.
